entries.title: [DRAFT] Fourth-deficit transfer without fourth-moment convergence
entries.statement: DRAFT conditional lemma: If real X_n converge in law, E X_n=0, E X_n^2=1 and E X_n^4<=3-epsilon for one fixed 0<epsilon<=2, then the limit X is centered, has variance one and E X^4<=3-epsilon, so it is non-Gaussian. Fourth-power uniform integrability is unnecessary: the fourth bound gives second-power uniform integrability, and Portmanteau bounds the limiting fourth moment. This does not supply an Ising deficit or field tightness.

entries.title: [DRAFT] Rejected first-moment shortcut
entries.statement: REJECTED INFERENCE: A diverging mean E N_n of a nonnegative overlap count by itself implies a scale-uniform positive probability P(N_n>0). The implication is false without an anti-concentration or relative second-moment premise, even when the count is finite at each scale.
assumptions: this entry labels a false inference; it is not a theorem

entries.title: [DRAFT] Rare-overlap counterexample
entries.statement: DRAFT counterexample to the first-moment inference: For integer n>=2, let N_n=n^2 with probability 1/n and zero otherwise. Then E N_n=n tends to infinity, P(N_n>0)=1/n tends to zero, and E N_n^2/(E N_n)^2=n. For any nonnegative witness N with 0<E N and E N^2<=C(E N)^2, Cauchy-Schwarz instead guarantees P(N>0)>=1/C. This is a logical counterexample, not an Ising-current construction.
assumptions: nonnegative witness; finite second moment for the sufficient bound

entries.title: [DRAFT] Exact endpoint-weighted bridge
entries.statement: DRAFT conditional current bridge: On a finite ferromagnetic Ising graph at finite beta, zero external field and free boundary, choose nonzero nonnegative f. Set G_xy=E sigma_x sigma_y, V=sum f_x f_y G_xy and mu(x,y)=f_x f_y G_xy/V. For positive-weight pairs sample independent currents with source sets {x} symmetric-difference {y} and {z} symmetric-difference {t}; q is the probability x is connected to z in their union, with reflexive connectivity. Repeated sources cancel. Then 3-E[(sum f_x sigma_x/sqrt(V))^4]=2 sum mu(x,y)mu(z,t)q(x,y,z,t). A witness's relative second-moment bound must hold under this endpoint-weighted law and for the original connection event. No critical 3D bound is supplied.

entries.title: [DRAFT] Enlarged-current event obstruction
entries.statement: DRAFT route obstruction: Adding independent sourceless currents enlarges source clusters and can give an upper bound on the exact two-sourced-current connection probability in the fourth-Ursell identity. A lower bound on the enlarged event cannot be reversed into a lower bound on the original event. A valid overlap witness for nontriviality must imply connection in the original union, or a separate quantitative comparison must be proved.
assumptions: exact original two-current event distinguished from enlarged clusters

entries.title: [DRAFT] Block deficit to source coupling comparison
entries.statement: DRAFT conditional comparison: In a translation-invariant, spin-flip symmetric zero-field Ising state on Z^3 assume U4<=0, 0<chi,xi<infinity and A=sum_{y,z,t} -U4(0,y,z,t)<infinity. Put g=-A/(chi^2 xi^3). For any nonempty finite block B, let M=|B|, S=sum_{x in B}sigma_x, V=E S^2>0 and R=3-E S^4/V^2. Then -g>=R V^2/(M chi^2 xi^3). Thus along beta_n increasing to beta_c, bounds R_n>=r>0 and V_n/[chi_n sqrt(M_n xi_n^3)]>=b>0 imply -g(beta_n)>=r b^2>0. These near-critical premises have not been proved for C0052.
assumptions: nonempty finite block with positive variance

relations.rationale: The explicit N_n family has diverging mean and vanishing positivity probability.
An actual uniform averaged connection lower bound gives a fourth deficit; the moment criterion then transfers it to any given weak scalar limit.
The weighted identity uses the original two-current event; the enlarged event cannot supply its lower bound without another premise.
Near-critical block deficits can be compared to the original infinite-volume source coupling when the explicit normalization premises hold.
